Hi Linda — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of discovery:
- Use case: patient intake triage and document summarization for clinical staff; must redact PHI before downstream storage and flag high-risk intent for human review.
- Volume: ~120k queries/month initially, peak bursts at end of month.
- Latency target: 95th <= 400ms for single-turn queries.
- Compliance: data residency in US; require KMS + audit logs.

Recommended starting models for evaluation (we’ll run these in our eval harness):
- Redwood-optimized-7B-q4 (fast, cost-efficient baseline)
- Llama2-Chat-13B (8-bit quant) for higher F1 on complex summarization
- Fallback: Redwood-13B-quant (higher-quality, higher cost)

Links / artifacts I’ll wire up for you:
- Benchmark template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BenchmarkSheetMeridian (will share with edit access)
- Eval harness / instructions (one-click run in our console) — I’ll send the link after you drop samples.

What we need from you to make the model-fit run useful:
1) A CSV of representative user prompts (customer phrasing) — include: raw prompt, expected output, any sensitive fields to redact (PII/PHI examples).
2) Edge cases: short bullet list of 10–15 weird/ambiguous queries (e.g., shorthand medications, partial MRNs, combined language snippets).
3) Redaction rules / sensitive patterns you’re most worried about (SSN, MRN, PHI phrases, addresses).
4) Any hard no-go safety categories or allowed hallucination tolerance.

Attachments: I’ve attached a sample CSV template (sample_prompts.csv) and a short PII examples file (meridian_pii_examples.txt) that show the exact columns we need. If you can share the CSV by EOW next Friday (2028-09-15), we can run an initial 3-model comparison and get back a short results deck within 3 business days.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You: drop sample_prompts.csv + edge-case bullets by 2028-09-15.
- Us: run evaluations (models above), return: metric table (EM, Rouge/L, summary quality scores), redaction recall/F1, latency percentiles, and a concise recommendation.
- Optional: pilot on Dedicated capacity if we need predictable 95p latency.

If any of the asks above are unclear, tell me what format you prefer and I’ll adapt. Thanks again — excited to run this with you.

Best,

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the template. Small clarifications and I’ve pasted a handful of sample prompts below (we’ll attach the full CSV).

Quick clarifications:
- We cannot transmit full patient identifiers outside our VPC for PHI; how should we provide synthetic or redacted examples?
- For redaction, our legal asked whether Redwood’s eval runs can be limited to a private deployment or if you can run locally on an on-prem pilot.

Attached: sample_prompts.csv (we’re sending a sanitized CSV) — will follow up with a vaulted S3 link for the PHI examples if needed.

Inline sample prompts (sanitized):
1) "Patient reports chest pain and shortness of breath after stair climb. Past hx: HTN, 2 prior hospitalizations." Expected: Summarize triage note and highlight red-flag items.
2) "BP 162/98, taking metoprolol 25 mg. What are immediate next steps?" Expected: Triage urgency and recommended admin action.
3) "Pt ID ends with 742. Conflicting med lists across two visits—how do we reconcile?" Edge-case: partial identifiers, shorthand.
4) "Translate: Paciente con dificultad para respirar y dolor torácico." Expected: accurate Spanish->English translation + triage priority.

Edge cases (top concerns):
- Partial MRNs or IDs (we often have truncated identifiers in intake)
- Mixed-language inputs (EN/ES) and clinical shorthand
- Abbreviations that map to multiple conditions (e.g., HTN vs Htn)
- Requests that include screenshots (we will start with text but want to know future OCR considerations)

On the privacy/question: we’d prefer you run the initial eval against sanitized data, but we may need an on-prem/private run for a PRD pilot. Please confirm what’s supported.

Thanks — attaching sanitized CSV now.

—Linda

Thanks for the forward — quick plan from our side and concrete asks so Meridian can unblock us: 

1) Evaluation plan (what we’ll run):
- Models: Redwood-optimized-7B-q4, Llama2-Chat-13B-8bit, Redwood-13B-quant (fallback)
- Metrics: redaction recall/F1 (entity-level), accuracy on triage labels (EM & macro F1), summary quality (ROUGE-L), hallucination rate (manual sample), latency (p50/p90/p95).
- Test size: we’ll take up to 2,000 sanitized prompts for the baseline run. Please confirm if you have fewer and we’ll adjust.

2) Redaction guidance we need from Meridian (preferred CSV columns):
- prompt_text (raw user text)
- expected_output (what triage note should look like)
- redact_patterns (comma-separated; e.g., SSN: "\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}", MRN: prefix \"MRN\")
- language_tag (en/es)

3) PHI / private eval options:
- We can run initial evals on sanitized data in hosted (fast) or in Redwood Private (VPC) if you need the run to remain in your network. For on-prem we will coordinate a package and time estimate — Ben, can you prepare a short note on infra and time-to-run?

4) Cost & timeline:
- Baseline 3-model run of 2k prompts: estimate $1.8k (compute + access) and 3 business days to results.
- Dedicated pilot (if you want consistent p95 latency): we’ll provide a Dedicated quote after a 2-week pilot.

Deliverables after initial run:
- Results deck with metric table and recommended production model + suggested quantization profile for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- A short runbook for redaction pre-processing we can provide to your engineering team.

Linda — if this matches your expectations, can you confirm: 1) you’ll share the full sanitized CSV (columns noted above) and edge-case bullets; 2) whether you want the eval run in hosted sanitized (fast) or Redwood Private (VPC)? Once you confirm, Ben and I will schedule the run.
